source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Having an extremely rapid onset of action that makes it well suited for treating emergent, severe episodes of hyperkalemia","B":"Has a relatively slower onset of action and is generally not relied upon as the sole treatment for severe, emergent hyperkalemia","C":"Carrying fairly little effect on the client's serum potassium level once the medication has actually been taken","D":"Being administered to the client only through the intravenous route rather than by mouth or as an enema"}}
source_row.rationale: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate has a relatively slower onset of action, so it is generally not relied upon as the sole treatment for severe, emergent hyperkalemia, which requires more rapid-acting interventions (such as calcium, insulin/glucose, or dialysis) alongside or instead of this agent.
source_row.source_detail: Onset of Action and Role in Emergent Hyperkalemia
